ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction strength B is perpendicular to the plane of the paper. There is a square, uniform metal wire frame abcd within the plane of the paper, with side length L and a total resistance of R. The side ad is parallel to the boundary of the magnetic field. Under the action of a pulling force to the left, the wire frame moves at a constant velocity v from the instant the side ad just enters the magnetic field until the side bc is about to enter it.

1. What is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force E?
2. What is the power P of the work done by the pulling force?
3. What is the Joule heat Q generated by the side ab?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction strength B is perpendicular to the plane of the paper. There is a square, uniform metal wire frame abcd within the plane of the paper, with side length L and a total resistance of R. The side ad is parallel to the boundary of the magnetic field. Under the action of a pulling force to the left, the wire frame moves at a constant velocity v from the instant the side ad just enters the magnetic field until the side bc is about to enter it. 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the left area of the figure, multiple “×” marks are drawn, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface inward; the right boundary of the magnetic field is a vertical dashed line. The square metal wire frame is located on the right side of the dashed line, with the left side being ad, the right side being bc, the upper side being ab, and the lower side being dc; ad is parallel to the magnetic-field boundary. The velocity arrow in the figure points to the left, indicating that the wire frame enters the magnetic field to the left. Reasoning: From when the ad side has just entered the magnetic field to before the bc side is about to enter the magnetic field, the area of the wire frame entering the magnetic field increases at the rate dS/dt=Lv. Therefore, the magnitude of the rate of change of magnetic flux is |dΦ/dt|=B·Lv, and by Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the induced electromotive force is E=BLv. The total resistance of the wire frame is R, so the induced current I=E/R=BLv/R. The wire frame moves uniformly, and the power of the work done by the external force is equal to the Joule heat power of the entire circuit, namely P=I^2R=B^2L^2v^2/R. The wire frame is uniform, and the total resistance is R, so the resistance of each side is R/4; the whole entering process lasts time t=L/v, so the Joule heat generated by the ab side is Q_ab=I^2(R/4)t=(B^2L^2v^2/R^2)(R/4)(L/v)=B^2L^3v/(4R).
